tuna-frittata.title: Tuna & spinach frittata
tuna-frittata.sub: A tender frittata with tuna, spinach, feta and lemon zest, topped with avocado.
equip: 20–24 cm nonstick skillet with a lid
ing: Salt, black pepper, garlic powder, chili flakes
steps: Finely chop the onion and dill. Drain the tuna and flake it with a fork.
Heat the skillet over medium heat and coat with oil. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Whisk the egg whites with mustard, lemon zest, salt, pepper, garlic powder and chili. Spread the tuna in the skillet, pour over the egg whites and sprinkle with feta.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cover. Cook without stirring until the center is set.
Sprinkle with dill, top with avocado slices and drizzle with lemon juice. Serve immediately.
tips: Low heat and a lid keep the egg whites tender rather than rubbery.
For a golden edge, remove the lid for the last 2 minutes.
tuna-frittata.store: Best fresh. Without avocado, refrigerate for up to 2 days; microwave for 40 seconds to reheat.
vary: Replace the tuna with 120 g cooked chicken breast.
Serve with sriracha or another hot sauce.

tuna-avocado-salad.title: Avocado tuna salad, no mayo
tuna-avocado-salad.sub: Mash avocado with lemon and mustard, then add tuna and a pickle. One bowl, no stove.
steps: Mash the avocado with a fork, lemon juice and mustard.
Add the tuna, finely chopped pickle, capers and onion. Mix and season with pepper.
Eat with cucumber rounds or in romaine leaves.
tips: Drain the tuna well: excess water makes the salad runny.
The capers and pickle provide plenty of salt.
tuna-avocado-salad.store: Eat the same day: avocado browns. Press plastic wrap directly onto the salad's surface.
vary: Replace half the avocado with 50 g nonfat Greek yogurt for less fat and more protein.
Add a pinch of smoked paprika or sriracha.

tuna-patties.title: Baked tuna patties
tuna-patties.sub: Mix everything in one bowl, spoon onto a baking sheet and bake. Serve with lime avocado and ready-made salsa.
equip: Parchment-lined baking sheet or air fryer
ing: Oil or cooking spray for the baking sheet
Salt, pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, chili flakes
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Squeeze excess liquid from the tuna and combine with all the patty ingredients in a bowl.
Spoon into 6 mounds and flatten to 2 cm thick.
Bake, flipping halfway through.
Mash the avocado with lime and salt. Serve with the patties and salsa.
tips: If the mixture is too wet, add a spoonful of oats.
Air fryer: 190 °C for 10–12 minutes.
tuna-patties.store: Refrigerate the patties for 3 days or freeze for 2 months.
vary: Use canned salmon instead of tuna for more fat and omega-3s.
Serve with cucumber and dill.

egg-white-muffins.title: Vegetable egg-white muffins
egg-white-muffins.sub: Twelve omelet muffins for the week, made with frozen vegetables and no chopping. Take them from the fridge and reheat for a minute.
ing: e.g. TJ Fire Roasted Peppers & Onions
Salt, pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, Italian herbs
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease the pan.
Microwave the vegetables to thaw them, then squeeze out excess water.
Divide the vegetables, spinach and feta among the 12 cups.
Whisk the egg whites with mustard, Parmesan and spices in the jug, then pour into the cups.
Bake until the centers are firm.
Cool for 5 minutes, then run a knife around the edges to release.
tips: Squeeze the vegetables well, or the muffins will be watery.
One serving is 3 muffins.
egg-white-muffins.store: Refrigerate for up to 5 days in a container lined with paper towel, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat for 45–60 seconds.
vary: Add 130 g tuna or turkey for another 30 g protein per batch.
Pizza version: tomatoes, oregano and a little Parmesan.

tuna-poke.title: Rice-free tuna poke bowl
tuna-poke.sub: Tuna, edamame, cucumber and avocado with soy-lime dressing and spicy yogurt.
steps: Cover the edamame with hot tap water to thaw, then drain.
Mix the soy sauce, lime, sesame oil and vinegar in one cup. Mix the yogurt and sriracha in the other.
Put the tuna, edamame, diced cucumber, avocado and cabbage in a bowl.
Drizzle with both sauces and sprinkle with sesame seeds and nori.
tips: Mix some dressing into the tuna to make it juicier.
tuna-poke.store: Assemble just before eating. The sauces keep for a week.
vary: Replace the tuna with 150 g cooked shrimp.
For a rice option, see Shrimp & edamame fried rice.

chili-lime-chicken.title: Chili-lime chicken with avocado
chili-lime-chicken.sub: Thin chicken breast pieces with spices and lime, cooked for 4 minutes per side. Serve with avocado and ready-made salsa.
ing: Paprika 1 tsp, cumin ½ tsp, ground chili ¼ tsp, salt ¾ tsp
steps: Slice the breasts in half horizontally into thin pieces. Skip this if using thin-sliced breast.
Rub with oil, lime juice, garlic and spices. Cook right away or let stand for 10 minutes.
Cook in a hot skillet for 4 minutes on each side.
Let rest, then slice.
Serve with avocado, salsa and lettuce.
tips: Thin pieces cook quickly without drying out.
Air fryer: 200 °C for 10 minutes.
chili-lime-chicken.store: Cooked chicken keeps for 4 days. Make 4 servings at once for the week.
vary: Use lemon and oregano instead of lime.
Slice into a salad or burrito bowl.

yogurt-chicken-salad.title: Rotisserie chicken salad with yogurt
yogurt-chicken-salad.sub: Ready-cooked rotisserie chicken, Greek yogurt instead of mayo, grapes and walnuts. No stove needed.
steps: Remove the breast meat from the rotisserie chicken and shred it by hand.
Mix the yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Add the chicken, halved grapes and celery, then mix.
Sprinkle with walnuts and eat from the bowl or in lettuce leaves.
tips: One Costco rotisserie chicken makes 2–3 servings.
yogurt-chicken-salad.store: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Add the walnuts just before eating.
vary: Use diced apple instead of grapes.
Curry version: add ½ tsp curry powder to the dressing.

garlic-shrimp-zoodles.title: Garlic shrimp with zucchini noodles
garlic-shrimp-zoodles.sub: Garlicky shrimp and cherry tomatoes over ready-made zucchini noodles. One skillet, 10 minutes.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry with a towel and season with salt.
Heat the oil over high heat and add the shrimp in a single layer.
Flip, then add garlic, chili and cherry tomatoes.
Add the zucchini noodles and heat through, stirring.
Drizzle with lemon juice and sprinkle with Parmesan.
tips: The shrimp are done when they curl into a C shape.
Keep the zucchini on the heat for no longer than 2 minutes, or it will release water.
Frozen shrimp thaw in about 5 minutes in a bowl of cold water.
garlic-shrimp-zoodles.store: Best fresh. Store the shrimp separately for 2 days.
vary: A spoonful of butter at the end makes a restaurant-style sauce (+50 kcal).
Use spaghetti squash instead of zucchini.

shrimp-ceviche.title: Ceviche with cooked shrimp
shrimp-ceviche.sub: Cooked shrimp, ready-made pico de gallo, lime, cucumber and avocado. Almost no chopping.
steps: Thaw the shrimp in a bowl of cold water and pat dry.
Cut the shrimp in half and dice the cucumber and avocado.
Mix everything with the pico de gallo and lime juice, then season with salt.
If time allows, let stand in the refrigerator.
tips: Ready-made pico already contains onion, tomatoes, cilantro and jalapeño.
shrimp-ceviche.store: Eat the same day. Without avocado, it keeps for up to a day.
vary: Add mango for sweetness (+30 kcal per serving).
Serve on lettuce leaves.

lemon-caper-cod.title: Cod with lemon, capers & tomatoes
lemon-caper-cod.sub: Oven-baked cod with cherry tomatoes and capers. The fish stays moist and makes its own sauce.
ing: Salt, pepper, a pinch of chili flakes
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and mix with capers, garlic, half the oil and salt.
Place the cod in the dish, season with salt and pepper, brush with the remaining oil and cover with lemon slices.
Arrange the tomatoes around the fish and bake until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (63 °C).
Drizzle with lemon juice, sprinkle with herbs and spoon over the pan juices.
tips: Thaw frozen cod completely and pat dry, or the dish will be watery.
Thick pieces take 16–18 minutes; thin pieces take 10.
lemon-caper-cod.store: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently for 30–40 seconds.
vary: Use the same recipe for tilapia, pollock or halibut.
Replace some capers with Kalamata olives.

fish-lettuce-tacos.title: Fish tacos in lettuce leaves
fish-lettuce-tacos.sub: Spiced fish, bagged cabbage with spicy yogurt, avocado and salsa in romaine leaves.
ing: Paprika, cumin and garlic powder, ½ tsp each; salt
steps: Pat the fish dry and rub with the spices.
Pan-fry for 3 minutes on each side.
Mix the yogurt with sriracha and lime, then stir half into the cabbage.
Flake the fish with a fork and divide among the leaves with cabbage, avocado, salsa and sauce.
tips: A dry fish surface browns; a wet one steams.
fish-lettuce-tacos.store: Store the fish and cabbage separately for up to 2 days. Assemble before eating.
vary: With shrimp: cook for 2 minutes per side.
Use chipotle instead of sriracha.

savory-cottage-bowl.title: Savory cottage cheese & vegetables
savory-cottage-bowl.sub: Cottage cheese with tomatoes, cucumber, herbs and a drizzle of olive oil. Five minutes and 30 g protein.
ing: 1% cottage cheese or low-fat farmer cheese
steps: Dice the tomatoes and cucumber, then chop the herbs and onion.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl and top with vegetables.
Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with pepper and seasoning.
tips: Everything Bagel seasoning replaces salt and adds crunch.
Use 2% cottage cheese if 1% tastes bland: +20 kcal.
vary: Add 50 g smoked turkey (+12 g protein).
Sweet version: berries, cinnamon and a spoonful of nuts.

skyr-berry-bowl.title: Greek yogurt with berries & walnuts
skyr-berry-bowl.sub: Thick Greek yogurt with a spoonful of protein powder, berries, walnuts and chia.
steps: Stir the protein powder into the yogurt until smooth. Add a spoonful of water if too thick.
Top with berries, walnuts and chia, then sprinkle with cinnamon.
tips: Thawed berries release juice that acts as a sauce.
skyr-berry-bowl.store: The yogurt and protein mixture keeps for 2 days. Add toppings just before eating.
vary: Chocolate version: chocolate protein powder and cocoa.
Replace the walnuts with 1 tbsp protein granola.

chocolate-protein-pudding.title: Chocolate protein pudding
chocolate-protein-pudding.sub: A thick chocolate dessert made with Greek yogurt, protein powder and cocoa. Prepare in 5 minutes, then chill.
ing: Sweetener, a pinch of salt, vanilla
steps: Mix the protein powder, cocoa and salt. Add the milk and stir into a smooth paste.
Stir in the yogurt and sweetener.
Divide between jars and refrigerate.
Serve with raspberries.
tips: Mix the dry ingredients with milk first, then add yogurt to prevent cocoa lumps.
vary: Add 1 tsp peanut butter (+30 kcal).
Mocha: add ½ tsp instant coffee.

green-protein-smoothie.title: Green protein smoothie
green-protein-smoothie.sub: Whey, spinach and avocado: a creamy texture, healthy fats and 30 g protein in a glass.
steps: Add the liquid to the blender, followed by spinach, avocado, banana, protein powder and ice.
Blend on high until completely smooth.
Taste and add lime or ice as desired.
tips: Liquid at the bottom helps the blender run smoothly.
green-protein-smoothie.store: Drink immediately. Avocado smoothies brown within a couple of hours.
vary: Add 100 g skyr for 11 g more protein and a creamier texture.
Add cucumber and mint for freshness.

turkey-lettuce-wraps.title: Turkey lettuce wraps
turkey-lettuce-wraps.sub: Lean ground turkey and mushrooms in a sweet-savory glaze. One skillet, with ready-minced garlic and ginger.
ing: Ginger paste or frozen ginger cubes
steps: Heat the oil over high heat and add the turkey and mushrooms.
Break up the turkey with a spatula and cook through.
Add the garlic and ginger, followed by the combined soy sauce, honey, vinegar, lime and sriracha. Reduce to a glaze.
Remove from the heat and add sesame oil. Spoon into lettuce leaves and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Mushrooms keep 99% lean ground turkey juicy.
Mix the sauce in a cup beforehand so you can pour it in all at once.
turkey-lettuce-wraps.store: Refrigerate the turkey mixture for 4 days. Store the leaves separately, wrapped in a towel.
vary: Use ground chicken breast instead of turkey.
Add rice for a full lunch (+185 kcal per 150 g).

burrito-bowl.title: Rotisserie chicken burrito bowl
burrito-bowl.sub: Ready-cooked brown rice, rotisserie chicken, black beans, corn, salsa and avocado. Just assemble.
ing: Nonfat Greek yogurt instead of sour cream
steps: Microwave the rice and corn.
Rinse the beans and season with salt and cumin.
Arrange the rice, beans, corn and chicken in a bowl.
Top with salsa, avocado, a spoonful of yogurt and lime.
tips: Buy enough rotisserie chicken and rice for 3 bowls.
Add sriracha or chipotle for heat.
burrito-bowl.store: Without avocado, an assembled bowl keeps for 3 days.
vary: Use tuna or cooked shrimp instead of chicken.
Replace the rice with quinoa.

salmon-sheet-pan.title: Sheet-pan salmon, sweet potato & broccoli
salmon-sheet-pan.sub: Sweet potato, frozen broccoli and salmon on one baking sheet, with a dill yogurt sauce.
ing: Salt, pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder
steps: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Cut the sweet potatoes into 2 cm cubes; no need to peel.
Toss the sweet potatoes with half the oil and the spices directly on the baking sheet, then roast.
Move the sweet potatoes aside, add the broccoli and salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil and season with salt.
Bake until the salmon flakes easily.
Mix the yogurt, mustard, dill and lemon juice.
tips: Salmon provides omega-3 fats.
Do not thaw the broccoli; put it straight on the baking sheet.
vary: Use baby potatoes instead of sweet potatoes.
Use cod instead of salmon: about 100 fewer kcal per serving.

protein-pasta-tuna.title: Protein pasta with tuna & cherry tomatoes
protein-pasta-tuna.sub: While the pasta cooks, sauté cherry tomatoes with garlic, tuna, capers and spinach. A sauce without cream.
ing: Salt for the water, chili flakes, pepper
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water according to the package. Reserve half a cup of cooking water.
Meanwhile, heat the oil with garlic, chili and cherry tomatoes in a skillet, crushing the tomatoes with a fork.
Add the tuna, capers and spinach, then heat through.
Stir in the pasta, a little cooking water and lemon. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
tips: Pasta water makes the sauce silky without cream.
protein-pasta-tuna.store: Keeps for up to 3 days; also good cold.
vary: Use shrimp instead of tuna.
Banza chickpea pasta adds more fiber.

overnight-oats.title: Protein overnight oats
overnight-oats.sub: Mix in a jar in five minutes at night; eat cold in the morning. Oats, yogurt, protein powder and berries.
equip: Jar or container with a lid
steps: Mix the oats, protein powder, chia and cinnamon in a jar.
Add the yogurt and milk, stir, then top with berries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
tips: Make 3–4 jars at once for the next few days.
Frozen berries thaw overnight and release their juice.
vary: Chocolate version: cocoa and chocolate protein powder.
Use apple and cinnamon instead of berries.

shrimp-fried-rice.title: Shrimp & edamame fried rice
shrimp-fried-rice.sub: Everything from the freezer: cooked rice, mixed vegetables, edamame and cooked shrimp. One skillet.
steps: Heat the oil over high heat and stir-fry the vegetables and edamame straight from the freezer.
Push to the side, pour in the egg whites and stir until set.
Add the rice, garlic and shrimp, then stir-fry.
Pour in the soy sauce and finish with sesame oil and sriracha.
tips: Cold rice fries better than freshly cooked rice and does not clump.
shrimp-fried-rice.store: Keeps for up to 3 days; reheat for 1½ minutes.
vary: Use rotisserie chicken instead of shrimp.
Add pineapple chunks.

chicken-hummus-wrap.title: Rotisserie chicken & hummus wrap
chicken-hummus-wrap.sub: A tortilla, hummus, rotisserie chicken and fresh vegetables. Five minutes, no stove.
steps: Spread the hummus over the tortilla.
Add the chicken, spinach, cucumber and tomato, then season.
Roll tightly and cut in half. If desired, brown in a dry skillet for a minute on each side.
tips: Hummus acts as a sauce and provides fats from chickpeas, tahini and olive oil.
chicken-hummus-wrap.store: Best assembled before eating; the filling keeps in a container for 3 days.
vary: Use tzatziki instead of hummus.
Add 20 g feta.

whey: Costco more often carries blends; look for 'isolate' on the label
harissa: TJ: Traditional Tunisian Harissa. Substitute: sriracha + smoked paprika
rotis: TJ carries sliced ready-cooked grilled chicken
zoodles: In the produce or frozen section
